slices.label: Nystad: Russia joins the great powers
events: Treaty of Nystad: Sweden cedes Estonia, Livonia and Ingria; Peter the Great is proclaimed Emperor of All Russia
London and Paris reel from the burst South Sea and Mississippi bubbles — Europe's first stock-market crash
Plague walls seal off Marseille as the last great western outbreak burns through Provence
slices.connectivityNote: Peace after two long wars reopens the Baltic grain run and Levant trade; Atlantic sugar-slave circuits boom despite the bubble crash.

entities.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
entities.note: Walpole steadies the ship after the Bubble; Hanoverian kings, Jacobite embers in the Highlands.

entities.name: Bourbon Spain
entities.note: Bourbon reforms centralize Castile and Aragon; Alberoni's Italian adventures just checked. Minorca and Gibraltar are British.

entities.name: Kingdom of Portugal
entities.note: Brazilian gold pours through Lisbon; John V builds Mafra.

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Regency for the boy Louis XV; Law's system has just collapsed.

entities.name: Duchy of Lorraine
entities.note: Duke Leopold rebuilds a land wedged between France and the Empire.

entities.name: Dutch Republic
entities.note: Still Europe's richest people per head, but the fleet and stadtholderless politics stagnate.

entities.name: Electoral Palatinate & Rhenish electorates
entities.note: Electoral patchwork of the middle Rhine: Palatinate, Cologne, Trier, Jülich-Berg.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire (Hanover & Lower Saxon states)
entities.note: Hanover shares its Elector with the British throne after 1714.

entities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
entities.note: Frederick William I drills the army and fills the treasury; Stettin gained from Sweden 1720.

entities.name: Electorate of Saxony
entities.note: Augustus the Strong, also King of Poland; Meissen porcelain and Dresden baroque.

entities.name: Landgraviate of Hesse & Franconian states
entities.note: Hesse-Kassel and the Franconian bishoprics; soldiers for hire.

entities.name: Austrian Habsburg Monarchy
entities.note: Charles VI at high-water: Naples, Sicily, Milan, Belgium, and Passarowitz's Belgrade and Banat.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sardinia (Savoy)
entities.note: Victor Amadeus II swapped Sicily for Sardinia in 1720 — a royal crown kept, an island changed.

entities.name: Republic of Venice
entities.note: Morea lost to the Turks in 1715; the Republic settles into neutral, carnival twilight.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
entities.note: The last Medici; the powers already haggle over the succession.

entities.name: Republic of Genoa
entities.note: Bankers to half of Europe; restless Corsica is the Republic's one territory of size.

entities.name: Knights Hospitaller (Malta)
entities.note: Crusading order turned corsair-policing anachronism.

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark-Norway
entities.note: Gained ducal Schleswig from the war; sound dues fill the treasury.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sweden
entities.note: Empire lost at Nystad; the 'Age of Liberty' hands power to the Riksdag.

entities.name: Russian Empire
entities.note: St Petersburg, a navy, Baltic provinces: Peter's empire faces west.

entities.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
entities.note: Ruined by the northern war and the liberum veto; a Russian protectorate in all but name.

entities.name: Crimean Khanate
entities.note: Last Chinggisid state; slave raids dwindle as Russia builds steppe lines.

entities.name: Principality of Moldavia
entities.note: Phanariot Greek hospodars now appointed from Constantinople.

entities.name: Principality of Wallachia
entities.note: Phanariot rule; Oltenia in the west held by Austria 1718-39.

entities.name: Ottoman Empire
entities.note: Tulip Era: peace, gardens and printing presses after Passarowitz's losses.

entities.name: Safavid Persia
entities.note: Afghan rebels march on Isfahan; the two-century Safavid order is dying.

entities.name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti (Georgia)
entities.note: Vakhtang VI of Kartli maneuvers between Persia's collapse and Russia.

entities.name: Alaouite Morocco
entities.note: Moulay Ismail's slave army holds the sharifian empire together.

entities.name: Regency of Algiers
entities.note: Dey and janissary divan rule under nominal Ottoman suzerainty; corsairing and ransom economy.

entities.name: Regency of Tunis (Husainid)
entities.note: Husainid beys, hereditary from 1705, trade as much as they raid.

entities.name: Regency of Tripoli (Karamanli)
entities.note: Karamanli dynasty autonomous since 1711.

relations.note: Nystad peace reopens the Baltic; Sweden buys back Finland with iron and tar
Stanhope-Dubois entente polices the Utrecht settlement
Adriatic and Levant commerce resumes after Passarowitz
Passarowitz commercial treaty opens the Danube
Naval stores and timber despite George I's Baltic jealousy
Marseille's Levant trade under the capitulations
Persia's collapse tempts the Porte into the Caucasus

slices.label: Silesia seized: Europe against Maria Theresa
events: Charles VI dies; Frederick II of Prussia invades Silesia in December — the War of the Austrian Succession begins
The Great Frost of 1740: Europe's coldest winter in memory brings famine from Ireland to the Ukraine
Britain and Spain fight the War of Jenkins' Ear across the Caribbean sea-lanes
slices.connectivityNote: Atlantic trade keeps climbing, but renewed continental war, privateering and a famine winter clog the arteries.

entities.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
entities.note: Walpole dragged into war with Spain; turnpikes and tobacco re-exports boom.

entities.name: Bourbon Spain
entities.note: Philip V's revived navy fights Britain; Italian thrones won for his sons.

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Fleury's long peace ends; Belle-Isle plots to dismember the Habsburg lands.

entities.name: Duchy of Lorraine
entities.note: Stanisław Leszczyński holds the duchy for life; it reverts to France on his death (1766).

entities.name: Dutch Republic
entities.note: Rentier republic: capital flows to London as the fleet rots.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire (Hanover & Lower Saxon states)
entities.note: George II's Hanover: a continental hostage for British policy.

entities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
entities.note: Frederick II seizes Silesia weeks after his accession — doubling Prussia's looms and taxpayers.

entities.name: Electorate of Bavaria
entities.note: Charles Albert claims the whole Habsburg inheritance.

entities.name: Austrian Habsburg Monarchy
entities.note: Maria Theresa, 23, inherits a bankrupt monarchy; Naples, Sicily, Belgrade and now Silesia gone.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sardinia (Savoy)
entities.note: Charles Emmanuel III auctions his alliance between Bourbon and Habsburg.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
entities.note: Habsburg-Lorraine since 1737: Francis Stephen traded Lorraine for the Medici inheritance.

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: Benedict XIV, the Enlightenment's favourite pope, elected this year.

entities.name: Republic of Genoa
entities.note: Corsica in chronic revolt since 1729; a German adventurer was briefly its king.

entities.name: Kingdom of Naples & Sicily (Bourbon)
entities.note: Charles of Bourbon rules from Naples itself — the south's first resident king in two centuries.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sweden
entities.note: Hats vs Caps party politics; the Hats itch for revenge on Russia (war 1741).

entities.name: Russian Empire
entities.note: Azov regained 1739; Zaporizhian Cossacks back under the Tsaritsa's hand since 1734.

entities.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
entities.note: Augustus III reigns from Dresden; the Sejm has not passed a law in years.

entities.name: Crimean Khanate

entities.name: Principality of Wallachia
entities.note: Oltenia recovered from Austria at Belgrade, 1739.

entities.name: Ottoman Empire
entities.note: Belgrade and northern Serbia won back in 1739 — the Porte's last victorious peace.

entities.name: Afsharid Persia (Nader Shah)

entities.name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti (Georgia)

entities.name: Alaouite Morocco

entities.name: Regency of Algiers

entities.name: Kingdom of Great Britain

entities.name: Bourbon Spain

entities.name: Kingdom of Portugal

entities.name: Dutch Republic

uncertainties: BLR assigned to Russia from 1772: only its eastern third (Polotsk-Vitebsk-Mogilev) went in the First Partition; Minsk stayed Polish until 1793. Rendered whole-cell Russian per era brief to make the Partition visible.
STE (lower-Dnieper steppe) given to Russia from 1740: the Zaporizhian Host returned to Russian allegiance in 1734, but the Yedisan coastal strip remained Ottoman/Nogai until 1774-91.
DON given to Russia from 1721 (Don Cossack Host under Petrine control) although era12 left it Crimean at 1714 after the Pruth; Azov itself was Ottoman 1711-39.
SAX shown Prussian (contested) at 1756: Frederick occupied Saxony from September 1756 and impressed its army; the Electorate is restored in the 1763 slice.
SIL shown Prussian at 1740 although the invasion came only in December of that year — per brief, to date the seizure.
Barbary regencies (Algiers, Tunis, Tripoli) split from the Ottoman entity from 1721: de facto autonomous under nominal suzerainty; matches era14's 1799 treatment. Cyrenaica bundled with Tripoli.
Egypt kept Ottoman throughout despite Mamluk-bey autonomy (Ali Bey al-Kabir's 1768-72 revolt noted at 1772).
LOM cell (Lombardy & Veneto) kept Venetian all century although Austrian Milan occupies its western edge — follows era12's convention; Austria's Milanese population counted in its total.
Minorca's British occupation (1708-82) and Gibraltar are sub-cell and not rendered; BAL stays Spanish (noted on Spain 1721).
Montenegro's de facto autonomy and the 1789-90 United Belgian States are too small/brief for whole cells; handled via notes and the FLA contested flag.

ARM cell: Safavid 1721 (collapsing), Afsharid 1740, then Erivan Khanate 1756-89 for the post-Nader fragmentation, Qajar from 1795 — the khanate was loosely tributary to Persia and at times to Erekle's Georgia.
Crimean Khanate keeps CRM (contested) at 1772 under Russian occupation; formal 'independence' 1774 and annexation 1783 fall between slices, so CRM turns Russian at 1789.
KAR kept Russian 1721-95 (East Karelia plus Kexholm/Vyborg ceded at Nystad and Åbo); era14 shows it Swedish at 1799, which conflicts, but the Russian assignment is the accurate one.
FRK kept with the Hesse entity through 1795 (Hesse-Kassel plus Franconian bishoprics; Prussian Ansbach-Bayreuth from 1791 noted); era14 folds it into a generic HRE entity at 1799.
France 1795 population (31M) includes annexed Belgium and the left-bank Rhineland; metropolitan France alone was ~28.8M.
Wahhabi expansion (Diriyah emirate, from 1744) stays off-map in Nejd; ARB flagged contested for Ottoman in 1795 for the first raids on the Hejaz fringe.
Jacobite risings (1715, 1745) fall between slice years; noted on Great Britain rather than rendered as separate control of SCO_N.
